lines.japanese: その後はなんとなく流れで、アロマキャンドルの香り漂うオサレ雑貨の店に連れていかれた。
lines.english: After that, one thing somehow led to another, and she dragged me into one of those trendy little gift shops that reek of scented candles.

lines.japanese: ちなみに「なんとなく」というのはこんな流れだ。
lines.english: For the record, here was the ‘somehow’ in question:

lines.japanese: 「隼人君、これからどっか行くの？」
lines.english: “Hayato, are you going somewhere now?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、どーすっかな、パチスロ屋でも行くかあ」
lines.english: “Hmm. What to do? Maybe I'll hit a slot parlor.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、何しに？　Ｔ借りに？」
lines.english: “What? Why? To use the restroom?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、何しにっておまえ、そんなんパチ屋行くつったら、パチ打つんだろよフツー」
lines.english: “What do you mean, why? When a guy says he’s going to a slot parlor, he’s going there to play the slots.”

lines.japanese: 「うん。でも隼人君の貧乏、フツーじゃないじゃん。娯楽にまわす余裕なんかないよ？」
lines.english: “Sure, but there's nothing normal about how broke you are, Hayato. You can't afford to blow money on fun.”

lines.japanese: 「ないよ？　じゃねえよ、てめーは経理か。お財布係か。俺のカミさんか。憶測でひとの出納管理すんな。しかも憶測当たってるじゃねえかコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Don't tell me what I can afford. What are you, my accountant? My treasurer? My wife? Quit managing my finances based on pure guesswork. And quit guessing right, asshole.”

lines.japanese: 「だしょー？　そうなの、隼人君お金にだけはシビアじゃーん？　ギャンブルで一攫千金とか夢見る系じゃあないっぽだよね」
lines.english: “Riiight? That's what I mean. Money's the one thing you're super serious about, Hayato. You don't seem like the type to dream about one big jackpot.”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　ああ、まあなァ。言われてみりゃ、そういう計画性のない射幸心は薄いかもなァ。まあそう、こう見えて意外と俺ァ、前を見据えてるっつうか自制が利くっつうか、んー、なんだつまり──」
lines.english: “Huh? Well, yeah. Now that you mention it, I guess I don't have much of that reckless gambling urge. Right. Believe it or not, I plan ahead. I exercise self-control. In other words, I'm—”

lines.japanese: 「けち」
lines.english: “Cheap.”

lines.japanese: 「──ひとを二文字で片付けんなよ」
lines.english: “—don't reduce a whole human being to one word.”

lines.japanese: 「ドけち？」
lines.english: “A total cheapskate?”

lines.japanese: 「悪化させんなよ」
lines.english: “Don't make it worse.”

lines.japanese: 「も、なーんでもい・だからなーんでパチンコ屋行くのってー」
lines.english: “Whatever, I don't ca—so why are you going to a gambling parlor?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、いや俺さ、このあとバイトなんだけど、集合までまだ時間あんだよ。だからホールの休憩所で雑誌でも読んでよーかと思って」
lines.english: “I've got work later, but there's still time before we're due to meet. I figured I'd sit in the lounge and read their magazines.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ～？　何ソレ、ちょっさーい。そんだったら私の買い物付きあってよ」
lines.english: “What? That's so lame! Come shopping with me instead.”

lines.japanese: 「ハァ？　なんでだよ。やだよ、めんどくせえ」
lines.english: “Huh? Why? No. Sounds like a pain.”

lines.japanese: 「いーじゃんいーじゃん。付きあってくれたらコレあげる、さっきもらったバーガーセットの割引券」
lines.english: “Come on, come on. If you do, I'll give you this burger-combo coupon I got earlier.”

lines.japanese: 「ハ、割引つったってそんなん、どうせ１０円２０円の世界だろ。そんなもんヤギの餌にしかなんねえって」
lines.english: “Hah. What's the discount, ten or twenty yen? That thing's fit for nothing but goat food.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、最大５０パー引きで２４０円もおトクだよ」
lines.english: “It's up to fifty percent off. You can save a whole 240 yen.”

lines.japanese: 「よし香田、今日から俺をヤギと呼べ」
lines.english: “All right, Koda. From this day forward, call me Goat.”

lines.japanese: という流れで現在に至ったわけだ。
lines.english: And that was how we arrived at the present.

lines.japanese: ローソク臭のするオサレ雑貨の店（看板の店名はヒョロヒョロした横文字で読めなかった）で、香田は化粧品だかプラモ用塗料だか、なんかそんなような感じのよく分からない瓶とかを買った。
lines.english: Inside the trendy little boutique that smelled of candles—the sign bore some spindly foreign name I couldn't read—Koda bought a collection of mysterious bottles containing either makeup or model paint or something along those lines.

lines.japanese: ローソク臭のするオサレ雑貨の店（香田は略称で呼んでいて聞きとれなかった）を出た俺たちは、ぼちぼち人通りの減りはじめた９時過ぎの歩道を並んで進む。
lines.english: We left the trendy little boutique that smelled of candles—Koda used some abbreviation for it that I couldn't catch—and walked side by side down the sidewalk. It was past nine, and the crowds had begun to thin.

lines.japanese: 「このあと、どするー？　ヤギはまだ時間あんの？」
lines.english: “What now? Does Goat still have time?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、まだ若干あんなあ。ていうか本当にヤギとか呼ぶのやめてくんない」
lines.english: “Yeah, a little. Also, could you seriously stop calling me Goat?”

lines.japanese: 「ぎゃー！　見てヤギ、何アレ何アレ、新機種ちょおカワイイかもー！」
lines.english: “Eek! Look, Goat! What's that? What's that? That new model might be super cute!”

lines.japanese: 「貼りつくな、ガラス壁に貼りつくな。あとヤギって呼ぶのやめてくんない」
lines.english: “Don't plaster yourself against the glass. And could you stop calling me Goat?”

lines.japanese: ケータイショップのショーケースから、ヤモリ状の小娘を引きはがした。しかしやつは俺の腕を抱きこんで踏みとどまる。
lines.english: I peeled the gecko-shaped girl off the phone shop's display window. She wrapped herself around my arm instead and held her ground.

lines.japanese: 「いいから見てみってー！　マジで超だし、すっごいホント、とにかくハイパーじゃん！」
lines.english: “Just look! It's seriously so, and totally really, and anyway it's, like, hyper!”

lines.japanese: 「っせえなあ。おまえの日本語、トッピングばっかで主食が……あれ、マジだ、かっちぇー」
lines.english: “Shut up. The way you talk is all toppings and no main course... Wait. Damn, you're right. That is cool.”

lines.japanese: 「ぎゃー！　見て見てあっちのも！　や～ちょっともうアレ、やり過ぎだってヤギ～」
lines.english: “Eek! Look, look, that one too! Oh my God, that is way too much, Goat!”

lines.japanese: すでに照明の落とされた暗い店先、俺たちは買う気もない携帯電話のフォルムやデザインについて、いちいちヤベーだのキテルだのと過剰反応して騒ぎたてた。
lines.english: Outside the darkened shop, its lights already off, we made an enormous fuss over the shapes and designs of phones we had no intention of buying, pronouncing each one ‘sick’ or ‘so hot.’

lines.japanese: そのとき黒瑪瑙のようなガラス壁に映っていた楽しげな男女は、まるでそこらの浮かれカップルと大差ないようにも見えた。そんなわきゃあねえ。
lines.english: In the black-onyx glass, the laughing man and woman looked almost exactly like any other giddy couple on the street. Yeah, right.

lines.japanese: 「そういや、話さっき途中で終わってたけど、そんで結局、森里どうしたつったっけ」
lines.english: “Speaking of which, we never finished that conversation. What did you say happened with Morisato?”

lines.japanese: 俺はどうでもいい他人の話をした。
lines.english: I brought up somebody I couldn't have cared less about.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、カズ君たちなら、さっきＬＲさんのワゴンが迎えにきて。みんなしてブォーンって、どっか遊び行っちゃった。良い子の亜衣ぽんは行かなかったけど」
lines.english: “Oh, Kazu and the others got picked up in LR's van earlier. Everybody went vrooom, off somewhere to have fun. Good little Ai stayed behind, though.”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん。みんなって誰」
lines.english: “Huh. Who's everybody?”

lines.japanese: 「いつものみんな。フレイムバーズの、だから翔さんとかバニィ君とか？」
lines.english: “The usual people. The Flame Birds—you know, Kakeru and Bunny?”

lines.japanese: 「ハ！　まーたアホが集まって、ロクでもねー集会してんのか」
lines.english: “Hah! The idiots are getting together for another worthless little meeting?”

lines.japanese: 「そーそ、集会ってか、なんか戦略会議たらゆっちゃってー？　きゃはは、バカデスネーって、どっかの不良チームと絶賛抗争中なんだってー」
lines.english: “Yeah, yeah. A meeting—or, like, they were calling it a strategy conference? Hahaha, what losers. Apparently they're in the middle of some glorious war with another street gang.”

lines.japanese: 「あーソレ、Ｒなんたらだ。いや、こいつらがまたロクでもねー連中でさ」
lines.english: “Oh, that's R-something. And they're another worthless bunch.”

lines.japanese: 「まじだー、もーいいよそんなのー。うちらはうちらでロクでもないことして遊んでよー？」
lines.english: “For real? I'm so over all that. Let's go do something worthless and have fun by ourselves.”

lines.japanese: 「だー、もう、いちいち触れんなっーの。すでにナウろくでもねー状態だっつーの」
lines.english: “God, quit pawing at me. We're already being worthless together, right here, right now.”

lines.japanese: ろくでもない小娘のろくでもないスキンシップを払いのける。そのはずみに、たまたま雑踏の中のろくでもない一人と視線がぶつかってしまった。
lines.english: I brushed off the worthless brat's worthless pawing. As I did, my eyes happened to meet those of one more worthless soul in the crowd.

lines.japanese: いかにも“オレ様かなりアナーキーだぜ”と主張したげなパンクルックの悪ガキが、客を誘う大道芸人みたいな薄笑いで露骨にこちらを凝視していた。
lines.english: A punk brat whose entire outfit proclaimed *Yeah, I’m one seriously anarchic bastard* was staring openly at us, wearing the thin smile of a street performer trying to draw a crowd.

lines.japanese: パイナップルを逆さまにして重油に浸したようなボサボサ頭。スカルのタンクトップにクロスのパーカー、下は傷だらけのダメージジーンズ──
lines.english: His tangled hair looked like an upside-down pineapple dunked in fuel oil. A skull tank top, a cross on his hoodie, distressed jeans slashed to ribbons—

lines.japanese: ──まただ。またひとり、あのアフリカ太鼓に群がっていたような、黒ずくめの信徒がここに。
lines.english: —again. Another black-clad believer like the ones who had swarmed around that African drum.

lines.japanese: 「ヴェエ～ッ！」
lines.english: “Bleeeeh!”

lines.japanese: そいつは鼻に深いシワを刻んだ好戦的なアッカンベエで、俺の無辜なる視線を押しかえしてきた。きっと、先に目を逸らした方が臆病者の烙印を押されるとでも思ってるんだろう。うへえ、おっかねえや。
lines.english: He answered my innocent gaze by scrunching his nose into deep furrows and sticking out his tongue with open hostility. He probably thought whoever looked away first would be branded a coward. Ooh. Scary.

lines.japanese: 「ああ香田さ、ちょっと聞きたいんだけど」
lines.english: “Hey, Koda. Quick question.”

lines.japanese: 臆病者で結構。俺は見知らぬパンクスの挑発をスルーするため、女へ向きなおって適当な話題をふった。
lines.english: Coward was fine with me. I turned back to Koda and threw out the first subject that came to mind, ignoring the strange punk's challenge.

lines.japanese: 「おまえアレ、最近背もたれ付きのチャリって見たことない」
lines.english: “Have you seen a bicycle with a backrest lately?”

lines.japanese: 「背もたれ？　あの、お母さんが後ろに子供乗せるみたいな？」
lines.english: “A backrest? Like the kind a mother puts behind the child seat?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、子持ちじゃねーと思うけど赤いの。赤くてなんか背もたれ付いてんの。そーゆーチャリンコ探してんだけど」
lines.english: “I don't think the owner has a kid. It's red. Red, with some kind of backrest. I'm looking for a bike like that.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、便利屋の仕事で？」
lines.english: “Oh. For a handyman job?”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、そういうわけでもねーんだけどさ。知ってるやつがソレ盗まれて困ってっから」
lines.english: “Not really. Somebody I sort of know had it stolen, and now they’re in a bind.”

lines.japanese: 「知ってるやつ……？」
lines.english: “Somebody you know...?”

lines.japanese: 「んー、まー、知ってるっちゃー知ってる感じのやつで」
lines.english: “Hmm. Well, somebody I sort of know, I guess.”
“...It's a woman.”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「女の勘が女だと告げている」
lines.english: “A woman's intuition tells me it's a woman.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、まーなぁ、男はあんま赤いチャリ乗んねーだろ」
lines.english: “Well, yeah. Men don't usually ride red bicycles.”

lines.japanese: 「認めた！　愛人の存在を認めた！」
lines.english: “He admits it! He admits he has a mistress!”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「子持ちママチャリ団地妻！」
lines.english: “A married mom from the apartment blocks with a kid seat on her bike!”

lines.japanese: 「きぃーっ！　私というものがありながら！　ありながら！」
lines.english: “Grrrr! When you already have me! You already have me!”

lines.japanese: 香田が両腕を振りまわす。俺はそのそよ風みたいな暴力に吹かれながら、同時に、へろへろ近付いてくる不穏な気配にも気付いていた。
lines.english: Koda windmilled both arms. As that gentle breeze of violence washed over me, I noticed an ominous presence weaving unsteadily closer.

lines.japanese: 「あ～ンのォ～！　ぷふっ、お楽しみ中のところスマっせぇーんハハ、ハハッ、ぶぁッハッハ！」
lines.english: “Ummmmm! Pfft, sorry to interrupt the fuuun! Hah, hah! Bwahahaha!”

lines.japanese: 手を伸ばせば胸倉を掴める距離で、あのパイン頭のパンク小僧が両手を叩いてカラ笑いしていた。落ちつきなく身をくねるたびに、耳たぶで安全ピンが揺れる。
lines.english: The pineapple-headed punk stood close enough for me to grab by the collar, clapping his hands and laughing without a trace of mirth. Safety pins swung from his earlobes every time he writhed.

lines.japanese: 俺と香田は互いに顔を見合わせ……そして各々の冷めきった表情から、そのキモい軟体生物がどちらの知己でもないことを確認した。
lines.english: Koda and I looked at each other... then confirmed from our equally dead expressions that neither of us knew this revolting invertebrate.

lines.japanese: 「はあ。べつにお楽しんでないんだけど、なに」
lines.english: “Right. We weren't having fun, but what do you want?”

lines.japanese: 「オウ、イェス！　プラマイゼロのいい表情！」
lines.english: “Oh, yes! Great faces! Plus and minus, dead even!”

lines.japanese: 男は指鉄砲をふたつこちらへ向け、照準を絞るように片目を瞑った。
lines.english: The man trained two finger guns on us and closed one eye as though sighting down the barrels.

lines.japanese: 「アちょっと？　ちょーっと聞きたいんだけどォ？　ぷハハ、おにーさんオオトリカケルのお友達だったりしちゃうワケぇ～？　ワケぇ～？」
lines.english: “Can I ask one little thing? Just one teeny thing? Puhaha! Is my man here perhaps a friend of Kakeru Otori? Perhaps? Perhaps?”

lines.japanese: 「ハァ？　おおおり？」
lines.english: “Huh? O-Otori?”

lines.japanese: 「ハじゃなくて！　ハじゃなくて質問にはイエスかノーでェ！　区役所の融通利かないジジイみたいにバッサリと容赦なくゥ！　例外は認めるなあああやややややばばばばばばファファファファファーック！」
lines.english: “Not ‘huh’! Not ‘huh’! Answer yes or no! Cut the case down without mercy, like some inflexible old bastard at city hall! No exceptions alloweeeeed—ya-ya-ya-ya-ba-ba-ba-ba-f-f-f-f-fuck!”

lines.japanese: 黒パインは電動バイブでも乗りうつったみたいに、全身でぶるぶるくねくね震えおどっていた。
lines.english: Black Pine shuddered and writhed in a full-body dance as though an electric vibrator had possessed him.

lines.japanese: 突然なんだよキモいな。香田も引いてる。俺もドン引き。通行人も目を逸らしてる。今日の俺はよくよく変なのに絡まれる日だ。
lines.english: What the hell was this? Creepy. Koda was backing away. I was backing all the way away. Passersby wouldn't even look at us. Apparently today was my day to be accosted by freaks.

lines.japanese: 「んイェス！　そんじゃまワンモァタイ、おにーさん、鳳翔のお・と・も・だ・ちィ～？」
lines.english: “Nnnyes! Then one more time! My man, are you Kakeru Otori's f-r-i-e-n-d?”

lines.japanese: 俺はしかめた顔を斜めに傾けながらも、馬鹿正直に答えてやった。
lines.english: I kept my scowling head tipped to one side and gave him a foolishly honest answer.

lines.japanese: <10>\「ウソは駄目えええぇーッ！！」
lines.english: “Lying is baaaaaad!”

lines.japanese: 耳元でアホの声が爆発した。しかもネギ臭かった。
lines.english: The idiot's voice exploded beside my ear. His breath smelled of green onions.

lines.japanese: 「だぁーめ！　ウソ言っちゃだめ゛え゛え゛ーッ！」
lines.english: “Baaad! You mustn't tell liiiies!”

lines.japanese: 「っせえな……なんだよいきなり……」
lines.english: “Shut up... What the hell is this, out of nowhere...?”

lines.japanese: 「あんた警察？　政治家？　マスコミ関係？　だァーンめよ、愚鈍なまでの正直さだけが市民の美徳でショ～、腐れた権力フェチの真似なんかしちゃ駄目だってェ！」
lines.english: “Are you a cop? A politician? The media? Noooo! Blind, stupid honesty is the citizen's one and only virtue! Don't imitate those rotten power fetishists!”

lines.japanese: やつは両腕をライダースのポケットに突っ込んだまま、駄々っ子みたいにどたどた地団駄を踏む。えらくテンションの高い不良だ。俺が無言で睨みかえすと、やつは膝を上下させてウッシャッシャと笑った。
lines.english: With both hands jammed into his biker jacket, he stamped his feet like a child throwing a tantrum. One remarkably excitable delinquent. When I glared back in silence, he pumped his knees and cackled.

lines.japanese: 「なぁ～ん！　だってほら、いまそれっぽい話してたジャ～ン、オオトリカケルがどうとかさァ。アごめんねェ、偶然聞こえちゃってェ会話」
lines.english: “Come oooon! You were just talking about him, weren't you? Kakeru Otori this, Kakeru Otori that. Oh, sooorry—your conversation just happened to fly into my ears.”

lines.japanese: 「ねェ教えてよォ！　キミ、クミトリカケルの仲間なんじゃないのォ？　汲み取り便所大好きカケルの仲間なんじゃないのォ？　汲み取った便をむしゃむしゃ大喰らいカケルの仲間なんじゃな～いののののののーッ！」
lines.english: “Tell me! Aren't you one of Kakeru Shithouse's little friends? One of Kakeru ‘Loves a Full Latrine’ Otori's little friends? One of Kakeru ‘Pumps It Out and Gobbles It Down’ Otori's little frieeeends?”

lines.japanese: ふざけた挑発に滲みでる攻撃性がより顕著になってきた。どうやら俺は、やつらの仇敵・柳木原フレイムバーズの一員だと思われているようだ。ひどい誤解。ひどい不名誉。
lines.english: The aggression bleeding through his idiotic taunts was becoming harder to miss. Apparently he had mistaken me for a member of the Yanagihara Flame Birds, their sworn enemy. A terrible misunderstanding. A terrible insult.

lines.japanese: 「違げえよ。バリクソ仲間じゃねえよ。そういうおまえはアレか、Ｒなんたらのやつか」
lines.english: “No. I am absofuckinglutely not one of them. What about you? You with R-whatever?”

lines.japanese: 俺は平静を装って後ろ頭を掻きまぜながら、過剰にへらへら笑っているパンク小僧の表情と、表情以外とを慎重に盗み見ていた。
lines.english: I pretended to be calm, scratching the back of my head while stealing careful glances at the punk's overdone grin—and at everything except the grin.

lines.japanese: 表面上はおどけた奇人を装ってるけど、末端神経──たとえば指の先──は決して油断していない。リズムを刻むような膝の屈伸だって、何かの準備態勢に見えなくもない。俺もやつに倣ってひそかに用心した。
lines.english: He played the clowning lunatic on the surface, but his nerves never relaxed—not even in his fingertips. Even the rhythmic pumping of his knees could have been a ready stance. I took the hint and quietly went on guard.

lines.japanese: 「ファック！　ご名答、よくご存知でェ！　さっすが八木君、汲み取りカケルの不快な仲間たちィ！」
lines.english: “Fuck! Correct answer! Well informed! Just what I’d expect from Goat, one of Kakeru Shithouse’s nasty little friends!”

lines.japanese: 「いや、だからマジで俺、鳳とかそんなん関係ないんだけど。あと、べつに名前じゃないからヤギって呼ぶのやめてくんない」
lines.english: “I'm telling you, I seriously have nothing to do with Otori. And quit calling me Goat. That's not my name.”

lines.japanese: 「んな～！　そんなそんな、隠さないでよ八木くぅ～ん！」

lines.japanese: そして、やつはすぐさま、残る手の袖口をナイフの上にかぶせた。物騒なおもちゃは、休日の夜を楽しむひとびとの視界から隠された。群集の中、俺とやつだけがにぶく光る切っ先を知っていた。

lines.english: “N-no... not really...”

lines.japanese: 「じゃ大丈夫じゃね？　一般人だてらに、やればできる子だから俺」
lines.english: “Then we’re probably good. I may be just a civilian, but I can do it when I put my mind to it.”

lines.japanese: 俺は硬直していた黒パインの鼻先でこぶしを開き、目潰しピースを突きつけてやった。
lines.english: I opened my fist at the tip of Black Pine's frozen nose and thrust an eye-gouging peace sign at him.

lines.japanese: 「……マジで」
lines.english: “...Seriously?”

lines.japanese: 「マジで。てめーらな、ちょっとばかし俺の目元がクールだからって、次から次へとインネンふっかけて来るとか冗談じゃねえぞ」
lines.english: “Seriously. Listen, you assholes. Just because I have such cool, brooding eyes doesn't mean you all get to come pick fights with me, one after another. I'm sick of this crap.”

lines.japanese: 「さっきも駅前で、おまえらの仲間に絡まれたばっかだよ。なにをそんなピリピリしてんだか、ほんと勘弁してくださいブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “One of your buddies already hassled me in front of the station. I don't know what has you all so wound up, but please give me a goddamn break or I'll fucking kill you, asshole.”

lines.japanese: 「あぁ、そう……だったんだ、ああ……」
lines.english: “Oh. Right... So that's... what happened. Yeah...”

lines.japanese: やがて、やつはパイナップルみたいな頭をわずかに垂らした。一応は謝ってるつもりみたいだ。ふてくされた森里みたいな顔をしていた。結局のところ、どいつもこいつも素顔はただの糞ガキだ。
lines.english: At last he lowered his pineapple head a fraction. Apparently that was meant as an apology. He wore the same sulky look Morisato got. Underneath it all, every last one of them was just a shitty little kid.

lines.japanese: 「それは……まあ悪かった、つうか、ごめん……いや、えっと、土下座でもした方がいいかな」
lines.english: “Then... yeah, that was my fault. Sorry. Um... should I grovel facedown on the pavement or something?”

lines.japanese: 「させてーぐらいだけど、人いっぱいいるからいい」
lines.english: “I'd love to make you, but there are too many people around.”

lines.japanese: そんなことされたって俺には一銭の得にもならない。それに昔じいさんがよく言っていた。
lines.english: It wasn't as though his groveling would put a single yen in my pocket. Besides, Grandpa used to tell me all the time:

lines.japanese: 汝の敵を赦せ。剣を持つ者はみな剣によって滅ぶ。世界が平和でありますように──
lines.english: Forgive your enemies. All they that take the sword shall perish with the sword. *May peace prevail on Earth*—

lines.japanese: ──まだ多感なお年頃だった隼人少年に、あのじいさんと来たら、来る日も来る日もそういうたぐいの説教をもっともらしく刷りこむものだから、いまや俺はすっかり心のにぶい大人に育ってしまった。
lines.english: —Day after day, that old man had solemnly hammered sermons like those into young Hayato at his most impressionable age. And so I grew into the thoroughly numb-hearted adult I was today.

lines.japanese: 「じゃ八木君さ、ちょっと時間あるかな、せめてディナーでもおごらせてほしいんだけど」
lines.english: “Hey, Goat. You got a little time? At least let me buy you dinner.”

lines.japanese: 「ハァ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: そう、だから俺がやつを許したのは、決して食欲に負けたとか財布が軽かったとか、そういう卑俗な理由からじゃあないんだ。たぶん。
lines.english: Right. So the reason I forgave him had absolutely nothing to do with surrendering to my appetite, or with the lightness of my wallet. Nothing so vulgar. Probably.
